1	# AI Insights
     2	
     3	A toolkit for structured, multi-agent AI development workflows. It gives AI coding agents a shared memory, a defined set of roles, and a headless execution path — so complex projects can be tackled across multiple chat sessions without losing context.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## 🧩 Tools
     8	
     9	### Agent Personas
    10	
    11	Pre-built prompt files that assign a specific role to an AI agent in your IDE (VS Code / Claude Code). Two suites are available:
    12	
    13	| Suite | Description | Docs |
    14	|-------|-------------|------|
    15	| **Ledger-Enabled** | 9-stage workflow (Planner → PM → Developer → QA → Security Auditor → Reviewer → Release Engineer → Docs → Synthesis) backed by the MCP server for persistent state | [personas/ledger/README.md](personas/ledger/README.md) |
    16	| **Standalone** | Single-purpose agents with no MCP dependency — drop in and use | [personas/standalone/](personas/standalone/) |
    17	
    18	### Project Ledger MCP Server
    19	
    20	A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that gives agents structured, persistent project state. It exposes 20 tools for managing work packages, tracking progress, and coordinating handoffs — with atomic writes and schema validation to prevent data corruption.
    21	
    22	→ [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md)
    23	
    24	### Orchestrator
    25	
    26	A headless, IDE-free alternative to the ledger workflow. Built on **LangGraph** + **Deep Agents**, it runs the same MCP-server-backed pipeline entirely from the command line — useful for automation, CI pipelines, or working outside an AI IDE.
    27	
    28	→ [orchestrator/README.md](orchestrator/README.md)
    29	
    30	---
    31	
    32	## 🚀 Quick Start
    33	
    34	```bash
    35	node scripts/cli.js
    36	```
    37	
    38	This opens an interactive menu where you can set up the workspace, sync personas, launch the GUI, run the orchestrator, and more — all from one place.
    39	
    40	Or run the full setup non-interactively:
    41	
    42	```bash
    43	node scripts/cli.js setup --all
    44	```
    45	
    46	You can also run any task directly:
    47	
    48	```bash
    49	node scripts/cli.js sync-personas          # build + deploy personas to IDE
    50	node scripts/cli.js gui                    # launch MCP GUI dashboard
    51	node scripts/cli.js orchestrator plan.md  # run orchestrator pipeline
    52	node scripts/cli.js ctx-generate          # generate context documentation
    53	node scripts/cli.js check-versions        # verify changelog vs manifest versions
    54	node scripts/cli.js read-log               # tail and query orchestrator logs
    55	node scripts/cli.js kill-orchestrator      # terminate stale orchestrator processes
    56	node scripts/cli.js kill-orchestrator --depth 5  # scan only 5 log files for lock cleanup
    57	node scripts/cli.js help                  # list all commands, grouped by category
    58	```
    59	
    60	> Commands are grouped in the help output by category: **Setup & Configuration**, **Validation & Utilities**, **Personas**, **MCP Server**, and **Orchestrator**. `read-log` and `kill-orchestrator` are available via direct dispatch but are not listed in the interactive help.
    61	
    62	> **Prerequisites:** Node.js >= 18. Python 3.11+ is only required for the orchestrator component. The `cli-menu` repository must be cloned as a sibling directory — see [Workspace directory layout](#workspace-directory-layout).
    63	
    64	Full setup and options for each sub-project:
    65	- [personas/ledger/README.md](personas/ledger/README.md) — Persona workflow guide
    66	- [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md) — MCP server architecture and GUI
    67	- [orchestrator/README.md](orchestrator/README.md) — Orchestrator setup, CLI reference
    68	
    69	---
    70	
    71	## 🛠 Development
    72	
    73	### Workspace directory layout
    74	
    75	The root `package.json` references `@mistralys/cli-menu` via a local `file:` path:
    76	
    77	```json
    78	"@mistralys/cli-menu": "file:../cli-menu"
    79	```

1	# WP-009: Route Wiring in `gui/server.ts`
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Implement the GUI Knowledge Page — 5 REST endpoints, route wiring, SPA view, API client methods, nav link, and CSS — completing the deferred Phase 6 from the Knowledge Accumulation System plan.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Wire the 5 knowledge REST endpoints into `gui/server.ts` — 3 body-free routes in `matchRoute()` and 2 body-parsing routes as special cases in `handleRequest()`.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/server.ts` — new imports for the 5 handler functions, `matchRoute()` additions, `handleRequest()` special-case blocks
    14	
    15	## Deliverables
    16	
    17	- Import block addition: `handleListKnowledge`, `handleUpdateKnowledge`, `handleDeleteKnowledge`, `handlePromoteKnowledge`, `handleMoveKnowledge` from `'./api.js'`
    18	- `matchRoute()` additions (before `return null`, after all project routes): `GET /api/knowledge` (with query string parsing for all filter params), `DELETE /api/knowledge/:id` (with `scope`/`project_slug` query params), `POST /api/knowledge/:id/promote` (with `scope`/`project_slug` query params)
    19	- `handleRequest()` special cases (before the final `matchRoute()` call): `PATCH /api/knowledge/:id` (with `readJsonBody`, full error handling for `PayloadTooLargeError`/`ApiError`/unexpected), `POST /api/knowledge/:id/move` (regex match on path, with `readJsonBody` and full error handling)
    20	
    21	## Dependencies
    22	
    23	- WP-001
    24	- WP-002
    25	- WP-003
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `GET /api/knowledge` is routed through `matchRoute()` and correctly parses all query string parameters (`scope`, `category`, `tags`, `project_slug`, `query`, `limit`, `offset`)
    30	2. `DELETE /api/knowledge/:id` is routed through `matchRoute()` with `scope` and `project_slug` from query string
    31	3. `POST /api/knowledge/:id/promote` is routed through `matchRoute()` with `scope` and `project_slug` from query string
    32	4. `PATCH /api/knowledge/:id` is handled as a special case in `handleRequest()` with JSON body parsing and proper error handling for `PayloadTooLargeError`, `ApiError`, and unexpected errors
    33	5. `POST /api/knowledge/:id/move` is handled as a special case in `handleRequest()` with JSON body parsing and proper error handling
    34	6. Route dispatch follows the established two-tier pattern: body-free routes in `matchRoute()`, body-parsing routes in `handleRequest()` special cases
    35	7. Knowledge routes do not interfere with existing routes (insights, projects, orchestrator)
    36	
    37	## Active Pipeline Stages
    38	
    39	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    40	
    41	## Estimated Complexity
    42	
    43	Medium
    44	
    45	## Rationale
    46	
    47	The two-tier dispatch selection (body-free routes in `matchRoute()`, body-parsing routes as special cases in `handleRequest()`) follows the established pattern documented in `gui/server.ts` comments and `file-tree.md`. Knowledge routes use the unique `knowledge` first segment, so no conflict with existing routes.
    48	
    49	## Notes
    50	
    51	Depends on WP-001, WP-004, and WP-005 (all 5 handler functions must exist). The `DELETE` response via `matchRoute()` returns `null` which `sendJson(res, 200, null, port)` sends as JSON — consistent with existing delete handlers that return 200 (not 204).

    22	- `handleMoveKnowledge` tests (6 cases): global to project, project to different project, VALIDATION_ERROR for same destination, VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid slug (path-traversal), NOT_FOUND for unknown id, scope disambiguation with same numeric id
